description: Single storey front extension, part single, part 2-storey side/rear extensions and conservatory to rear.
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location PlanBlock Plan 1782/011782/021782/031782/041782/051782/061782/071782/081782/09Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that match the existing building or as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a full specification and installation methodology for the foundations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The specification shall demonstrate adherence to the guidelines set out in NHBC Chapter 4.2 Building near Trees.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the development will be adequately constructed against a risk of future subsidence and to ensure that off site trees of high amenity value and public benefit will not be at risk through implication in possible future subsidence cases, in accordance with Policy DMD80(b) (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of the off site trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a tree survey, a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures. Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:1.	location and installation of all utility services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retained trees (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);2.	methods of demolition of existing structures within or directly adjacent to RPAs and the removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;3.	site specific methodology for the foundation installation and all associated works with RPAs;4.	details of all construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs;5.	a full specification for the construction of all paths, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the existing layout of hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;6.	detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;7.	a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;8.	a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;9.	a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);10.	details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;11.	methods to improve the rooting environment for retained and proposed trees and landscaping. The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details. Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
